tier_reason: First-party numbers only. The master readme.md table (win/mac/linux, co/json vs rapidjson) matches the record exactly; the benchmark code (benchmark branch benchmark/json_bm.cc with benchmark/rapidjson.h) is public, but no CPU model or compiler version is stated anywhere, and the README table itself does not appear in any benchmark-branch results file.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Benchmark branch benchmark/xmake.lua builds json_bm with set_optimize("fastest") (per the top-level xmake.lua comments: -O3 on gcc/clang, -Ox on MSVC); libco itself is built by the top-level xmake.lua with set_optimize("fastest") and /MT on Windows but set_optimize("faster") (-O2) on Linux/macOS; C++11; RAPIDJSON_SSE42 defined only if CO_SSE42 is set. Compiler names and versions not stated.
corrections.claimed_speedup: master readme.md table (us, co/json vs rapidjson, minified twitter.json): win stringify 569 vs 2089 (3.6x), parse 924 vs 2495 (2.7x); mac stringify 783 vs 1289 (1.6x), parse 1097 vs 1658 (1.5x); linux stringify 468 vs 1359 (2.9x), parse 764 vs 1070 (1.4x). The benchmark branch top-level readme.md also compares simdjson (parse / stringify / parse(minimal) / stringify(minimal), us): linux rapidjson 1233.701 / 2503 / 1057.799 / 2243, simdjson 385.3 / 1779 / 351.752 / 2298, co/json 666.979 / 1660 / 457.381 / 981; windows rapidjson 4197.339 / 3008 / 4078.067 / 2216, simdjson 843.06 / 2373 / 607.946 / 2119, co/json 717.444 / 1514 / 623.745 / 993. The benchmark branch benchmark/readme.md gives a third set without simdjson: linux rapidjson 1270 / 2106 / 1127 / 1358 vs co/json 1005 / 920 / 788 / 470; windows rapidjson 4260 / 2472 / 4098 / 2831 vs co/json 1071 / 881 / 943 / 700.
corrections.caveats: First-party, partial methodology, so tier C. Table is identical to the v3.0.2 README (tag 2023-11-23), so it predates coost 4.0.0 (tag 2026-09-15) whose API changed (json::any, co::string); master test/jbm.cc now times only co/json, and the RapidJSON/simdjson comparison code is only on the old benchmark branch (last updated 2023-12-09; co::Json, fastring; its top-level readme.md still contains unresolved git merge-conflict markers). The README calls the figures averages, but in benchmark/json_bm.cc the stringify figure is a single timed call after one warm-up, while parse is the mean of 1000 loops. RapidJSON baseline is default Document::Parse with default flags (no in-situ, no SIMD unless CO_SSE42) and its stringify includes building a StringBuffer and copying into std::string. The harness also handicaps simdjson: it constructs a new simdjson::dom::parser inside every parse iteration (re-allocating its buffers each time, against simdjson's documented reuse pattern) and stringifies through std::ostringstream. Even so, simdjson parses faster than co/json on Linux (385.3 vs 666.979 us); co/json is faster only on the Windows run (717.444 vs 843.06 us), where RapidJSON is also about 3.4x slower than on Linux. README and benchmark-branch files give three different numbers for the same rows (e.g. linux parse 764 vs 1070 in the README, 1005 vs 1270 in benchmark/readme.md, 666.979 vs 1233.701 in the branch readme), and benchmark/readme.md says its Linux log numbers came from the Windows Linux subsystem. No CPU, compiler version or RAM stated.

notes: Record accurate; numbers verified on master readme.md and on both benchmark-branch readme files, harness verified in benchmark/json_bm.cc. Shortcomings: first-party, no CPU/compiler, single-shot stringify timing, simdjson handicapped by per-iteration parser construction yet still faster on Linux, numbers from pre-4.0 code that no longer has the comparison harness on master.
